title: E2B Alternatives for AI Agents: GPU and CPU Sandboxes Compared
summary: Compare the best e2b alternatives for AI agents: GPU and CPU sandboxes, isolation, session limits, persistence and per-hour pricing side by side.
body_markdown:
The best E2B alternative depends on what your agent is missing:


- **GPU workloads:** Thunder Compute
- **Long-lived state:** Daytona or Blaxel
- **Running in your own cloud:** Northflank or Runloop
- **Agents that mostly wait on model calls:** Vercel Sandbox or Cloudflare Sandbox SDK


E2B remains a strong default for short CPU-only tasks on open-source infrastructure.


**Takeaways**


- **E2B has no GPU sandboxes** ; Thunder Compute, Modal, Daytona, Northflank and Beam do.
- **A 2 vCPU / 4 GiB sandbox costs $0.07-$0.34/hr** at different providers and $0.17/hr at E2B.
- **[Active-CPU billing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/2025-11-21-new-cpu-pricing/)** from Vercel, Cloudflare and Fly.io Sprites cuts costs for agents waiting on LLMs.
- **Daytona, Blaxel, CodeSandbox SDK and Fly.io Sprites** keep state between sessions with fewer limits than E2B Hobby.
- **Northflank, Runloop, Beam and Daytona offer BYOC** ; E2B reserves bring-your-own-cloud for Enterprise.


## What E2B Is and What It Does Well


E2B is a cloud sandbox to run AI-generated code in isolated Linux environments. Its SDKs let an agent start a sandbox, run code and read results in a few calls. Additionally, E2B offers desktop sandboxes for computer-use agents. E2B reported[more than 2B cumulative sandbox launches in October 2026](https://e2b.dev/about) .


E2B stands out for strong isolation, pause and resume with full memory state, and open-source infrastructure. For short-lived, CPU-bound code execution, E2B is a solid baseline for comparing sandbox providers.


### How E2B Isolates Code With Firecracker MicroVMs


E2B gives each sandbox its own lightweight virtual machine and kernel, using Firecracker microVMs (AWS's open-source virtual machine monitor). A standard container shares the host kernel instead. Firecracker is the[same isolation approach AWS built for Lambda](https://www.usenix.org/conference/nsdi20/presentation/agache) . It is generally considered stronger than plain container isolation for untrusted code.


E2B limits an agent's ability to probe internal networks by[blocking outbound traffic to private and link-local address ranges](https://docs.e2b.dev/network/restrict-public-access) . It runs in five regions: US-West-1, US-West-2, US-East-1, EU-West-1 and AP-Southeast-1. Compliance claims include[SOC 2 Type II](https://e2b.dev/security) .


### Is E2B Free? E2B Pricing Explained


[E2B pricing](https://e2b.dev/pricing) combines a free Hobby tier with per-second billing on allocated resources. The Hobby plan includes a one-time $100 credit, sessions of up to one hour, and 10 GiB of storage. Usage costs $0.0504/vCPU-hour and $0.0162/GiB-hour of memory, billed on allocated wall-clock time. E2B[billing stops when a sandbox is paused, killed or times out](https://docs.e2b.dev/billing) .


E2B's paid tiers increase limits, but don't provide compute:


- **Pro** costs $150/month plus usage, with 24-hour sessions and 100 concurrent sandboxes.
- **Pro+** ($650/month) adds 500 concurrent sandboxes.
- **Pro++** ($1,150/month) adds 1K concurrent sandboxes.
- **Enterprise** starts at a[$3,000 monthly minimum](https://pricing.e2b.dev/) .

## Why Teams Look for E2B Alternatives


Teams evaluating E2B alternatives often need one specific capability rather than a wholesale replacement. Four recurring reasons drive the switch:


- GPU access
- Longer or more concurrent sessions without subscription plans
- Persistent state
- Control over where the infrastructure runs


### Your Agent Needs a GPU


[E2B does not offer](https://docs.e2b.dev/faq/gpu-support)[GPU sandboxes](https://www.thundercompute.com/blog/what-are-gpu-sandboxes) , so any agent step that needs CUDA must run elsewhere. The gap affects agents that fine-tune small models, run local inference, render, or run data-science code that assumes a GPU.


> [Request access to Thunder Compute GPU Sandboxes](https://www.thundercompute.com/products/sandboxes/request-access) to power your agents with H100 GPUs starting at $2.95/hr.


### Session Limits and Concurrency at High Volume


E2B[caps sessions at one hour on Hobby and 24 hours on Pro](https://docs.e2b.dev/faq/sandbox-lifetime) . Multi-day sessions are reserved for Enterprise. E2B concurrency starts at 10 sandboxes on Hobby and 100 on Pro upgradeable up to 1.1K.


Several E2B alternatives remove the session cap entirely:


- **Thunder Compute** runs sandboxes until deleted or timed-out.
- **Daytona** has no maximum session, only a configurable auto-stop.
- **Blaxel, CodeSandbox SDK and Fly.io Sprites** sleep or hibernate when idle.


For concurrency, Vercel Pro allows 10K sandboxes and Modal Team allows 5K containers.


### Persistence and State Between Sessions


E2B handles persistence well:[pause and resume captures memory and filesystem, and paused state is kept indefinitely](https://docs.e2b.dev/sandbox/persistence) . Teams usually switch from E2B for a different persistence model, not a missing one.


- **Blaxel** resumes full memory and process state in about 25 ms after auto-standby.
- **Vercel Sandbox** is persistent by default and snapshots the filesystem on every stop.
- **Fly.io Sprites** give each sandbox a persistent 100 GB filesystem with fast checkpoints.
- **Daytona VMs** support pause, snapshots and fork.


### Self-Hosting and Running in Your Own Cloud


E2B is one of the few sandboxes you can fully self-host. Its infrastructure is[Apache-2.0 licensed](https://github.com/e2b-dev/infra) and runs on GCP, AWS, Azure or Kubernetes.[Managed bring-your-own-cloud (BYOC) deployment on AWS, GCP and Azure](https://docs.e2b.dev/byoc) is available on Enterprise only.


Four E2B alternatives offer own-cloud options:


- **Northflank** offers self-serve BYOC across AWS, GCP, Azure, Oracle, CoreWeave, Civo, bare metal and on-prem.
- **Beam** offers BYOC and a self-hostable AGPL-3.0 engine called beta9.
- **Runloop** offers Deploy to VPC on Enterprise.
- **Daytona** offers custom regions where you run the runners.


Modal, Vercel, Cloudflare, CodeSandbox SDK and Fly.io Sprites are managed-only.

## The Best E2B Alternatives


Each E2B alternative below is compared with E2B on isolation, GPU support, session limits, persistence and pricing.


### Thunder Compute (Best for GPU Workloads)


Thunder Compute adds the GPU sandboxes E2B lacks, with the same Firecracker microVM isolation model as E2B. Thunder Compute offers an A100 80GB at $1.95/hr and an H100 at $2.95/hr, both non-preemptible. vCPU, memory and storage are billed on top.


Thunder Compute sandboxes are ephemeral, with no documented snapshot, pause or volumes. The default timeout is 300 seconds; it is configurable or can be disabled with` timeout=None` .


### Modal Sandboxes


Modal offers GPU sandboxes from T4 to B300, which is the biggest difference when comparing e2b vs modal sandboxes. Its sandboxes default to gVisor isolation (Google's user-space kernel). Full VM sandboxes are in beta for CPU-only workloads, since VM sandboxes do not support GPUs.


Modal's[GPU sandboxes are preemptible only](https://modal.com/docs/guide/sandbox-resources) .[GPU rates run from $0.59 per hour for a T4 to $7.10 for a B300](https://modal.com/pricing) , with CPU and memory billed separately. GPU concurrency is 10 on Starter and 50 on Team.


[Modal sessions default to 5 minutes and run up to 24 hours](https://modal.com/docs/guide/sandboxes) , matching E2B Pro without a plan fee. Modal persistence comes through Volumes ($0.09/GiB-month, 1 TiB free per month) and filesystem and memory snapshots. Concurrency reaches 100 containers on Starter and 5K on Team.


On Modal, region selection adds a 1.15x to 1.75x multiplier.


### Daytona


Daytona offers the widest choice of environments:[Linux containers by default, plus Linux VMs, Windows VMs and macOS on dedicated Apple silicon](https://www.daytona.io/docs/sandboxes) . Comparing e2b vs daytona isolation, E2B puts every sandbox in a microVM, while Daytona defaults to a container unless you choose a VM.


Daytona has no maximum session. Sandboxes auto-stop after 15 minutes of inactivity by default, and setting auto-stop to 0 keeps them running. Daytona containers keep their filesystem when stopped and can be archived or snapshotted.[Linux VMs add memory-preserving pause, resume and fork](https://www.daytona.io/docs/en/sandboxes/vm-sandboxes) .


Daytona's[Linux rates match E2B at $0.0504 per vCPU-hour and $0.0162 per GiB-hour](https://www.daytona.io/pricing) .


Daytona GPU sandboxes have two pricing tiers: on-demand for reserved hardware or spot that can terminate without notice. GPU options are H100, H200, B200, B300, RTX PRO 6000, L40S, RTX 4090, RTX 5090 and AMD MI355X. Daytona GPU sandboxes[are deleted on stop](https://www.daytona.io/docs/en/sandboxes/gpu-sandboxes) , with only filesystem snapshots available, and the $200 signup credit does not cover them.


### Vercel Sandbox


Vercel Sandbox matches E2B's isolation, running each sandbox in a Firecracker microVM with a dedicated kernel. Vercel Sandbox does not offer GPUs.


Vercel Sandbox differs from E2B mainly on billing.[Vercel charges $0.128 per vCPU-hour only for active CPU](https://vercel.com/docs/sandbox/pricing) , so I/O wait, including time spent waiting on AI model calls, is free. Memory costs $0.0212/GB-hour for the full session, plus $0.60 per 1M sandbox creations. For an agent that mostly waits on an LLM, Vercel can undercut E2B despite a higher list rate.


Vercel sessions run up to 45 minutes on Hobby and 24 hours on Pro, and the clock resets on each stop and resume. Sandboxes are[persistent by default, with filesystem snapshots on stop](https://vercel.com/docs/sandbox/concepts/persistent-sandboxes) and forking. Memory snapshots are not documented. Vercel Pro allows 10K concurrent sandboxes across[19 regions](https://vercel.com/docs/sandbox/concepts/regions) .


### Cloudflare Sandbox SDK


Cloudflare Sandbox SDK gives isolation comparable to E2B and integrates tightly with Cloudflare's developer platform. The SDK[runs each container in its own VM](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/architecture) and orchestrates it from Workers (Cloudflare's serverless platform) through a TypeScript SDK. Cloudflare offers no GPU sandboxes.


Cloudflare bills CPU on active use only.[Pricing is $0.072 per vCPU-hour of active CPU and $0.009 per GiB-hour](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/pricing/) for provisioned memory while running, billed in 10 ms increments. Disk costs about $0.00025/GB-hour. A Workers Paid plan ($5/month) is required.


[Instances top out at 4 vCPU and 12 GiB](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/platform/limits/) , smaller than E2B's 128 vCPU maximum. Account-wide limits on Workers Paid reach 1.5K vCPU.


Cloudflare has no hard session cap, but[sandboxes sleep after 10 minutes of inactivity](https://developers.cloudflare.com/sandbox/configuration/sandbox-options/) unless` keepAlive` is set. Disk and processes are lost on sleep. Persistence relies on[backups to R2 (3-day TTL)](https://developers.cloudflare.com/sandbox/api/backups) , Cloudflare's object storage, or on[container snapshots, which are in public beta](https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-09-30-snapshots/) .


### Runloop


Runloop focuses on coding-agent benchmarking and reinforcement learning, while E2B targets general code execution. Runloop's Devboxes are microVM sandboxes built for benchmarks such as SWE-Bench (a coding-agent benchmark). Neither Runloop nor E2B offers GPUs.


[Runloop charges $0.108 per CPU-hour and $0.0252 per GB-hour](https://runloop.ai/pricing) on wall-clock time. Sizes run from 0.5 CPU / 1 GB to 8 CPU / 32 GB, with custom sizes up to 16 cores. Runloop does not define whether a "CPU" equals a vCPU, which affects price comparisons.


Runloop sessions default to one hour and are configurable. Persistence includes disk snapshots and branching. Suspend and resume, which charge only for storage, requires the Pro plan ($250/month). Like E2B, Runloop offers deployment into your own VPC on Enterprise across AWS, GCP and Azure.


### Northflank


Northflank offers on-demand GPU sandboxes: RTX PRO 6000, H100, H200, B200, A100 (40 GB and 80 GB) and L4. Northflank is a general cloud platform with a sandbox product. CPU sandboxes run in microVMs (Kata Containers with Cloud Hypervisor, or Firecracker where nested virtualization is available). GPU sandboxes on Northflank cloud use gVisor by default.


Northflank has no session time limits, and sandboxes run until deleted. Sandboxes are ephemeral by default or persistent with an attached volume. Maximum size reaches 288 vCPU and 2 TB of memory.


Northflank charges[$0.01667 per vCPU-hour and $0.00833 per GB-hour](https://northflank.com/pricing) . Northflank's standout is self-serve BYOC across AWS, GCP, Azure, Oracle, CoreWeave, Civo, bare metal and on-prem. BYOC adds $0.02083 per node vCPU-hour on top of your cloud bill.


### Blaxel


Blaxel focuses on near-instant resume for stateful agents. Blaxel sandboxes auto-standby about 5 seconds after network inactivity. They resume in about 25 ms with full memory, filesystem and process state, a more aggressive model than E2B's manual pause and resume. Sessions are unlimited, and standby bills storage only.


Blaxel uses microVM isolation and does not offer GPUs. Pricing is set by memory tier with bundled CPU,[from XS (2 GB, $0.0828 per hour) to XL (32 GB, $1.3248 per hour)](https://blaxel.ai/pricing) . The S tier matches E2B's cost for a comparable size at $0.1656/hr. BYOC is available through sales, and new accounts get up to $200 of free credits.


[Baseten acquired Blaxel](https://www.baseten.co/blog/blaxel-is-joining-baseten-to-build-the-future-of-agentic-cloud/) in September 2026 and plans to launch Sandboxes built on Blaxel. Blaxel pricing and product details could still change after the acquisition.


### Beam


Beam is one of the few E2B alternatives covering both CPU sandboxes and GPU work. Beam offers a broad set of runtimes in one product:


- gVisor containers by default
- MicroVMs for CPU-only workloads
- GPU sandboxes on its container runtime
- Persistent VMs


Beam GPU sandboxes do not get microVM isolation.


[Performance-tier pricing is $0.05 per vCPU-hour and $0.01 per GiB-hour](https://www.beam.cloud/pricing) , billed per millisecond. Cheaper Shared and interruptible Spot tiers are also available. Beam does not bill image pulls, cold starts or egress. The Developer plan costs $20/month with $20 in monthly credits, and Team costs $89/month plus usage.


Beam sessions can run until terminated. Persistence includes memory and filesystem snapshots that can fan out to many sandboxes, plus volumes. Beam supports BYOC on AWS, GCP and Azure and can be self-hosted through its AGPL-3.0 beta9 engine, though not every cloud feature is included.


### CodeSandbox SDK


CodeSandbox SDK is built around hibernation and forking, on Firecracker microVMs like E2B. Hibernated sandboxes save memory and disk and resume in about 0.5-2 seconds. Live forks let an agent branch a running environment. CodeSandbox SDK offers no GPU sandboxes.


CodeSandbox[pricing works out to $0.0446 per vCPU-hour and $0.0149 per GB-hour](https://codesandbox.io/docs/sdk/pricing) , derived from VM credits and billed per minute, rounded up. The free Build plan includes 40 VM-hours per month, and Scale costs $170/month per workspace. Concurrency reaches 250 on Scale, and the largest size is 64 cores and 128 GB on Enterprise.


[Together AI acquired CodeSandbox in December 2024](https://siliconangle.com/2024/12/12/together-ai-acquires-codesandbox-adds-code-interpreter-ai-development-platform) .[Together's docs mark this SDK as legacy](https://docs.together.ai/docs/together-code-sandbox-legacy) , with together-sandbox as its successor at the same per-unit rates. No end-of-life date has been published.


### Fly.io Sprites


Fly.io Sprites behave like durable machines that sleep when idle, while E2B treats a sandbox as a task runner. Each Sprite is a persistent Firecracker microVM Linux computer with its own HTTPS URL and a 100 GB filesystem.


Fly.io Sprites have the most usage-based billing of these E2B alternatives. Sprites cost $0.0385 per CPU-hour of CPU actually used and $0.021875 per GB-hour of memory actually used, after a[price cut effective October 1, 2026](https://fly.io/pricing-update/) . Sleeping Sprites incur no compute charge.


Sprites have no session cap. Checkpoints take about a second but capture files, not running processes. Sizes top out at 8 vCPU and 16 GB, and[concurrency is up to 3 running Sprites on pay-as-you-go, or 10 on the $20-per-month Level 10 plan](https://docs.sprites.dev/reference/billing) .


## E2B Alternatives for GPU Agent Workloads


GPU access is the gap where E2B offers no option. For a wider provider list, see Thunder Compute's guide to the[best GPU sandboxes](https://www.thundercompute.com/blog/best-gpu-sandboxes-ai-agents) .


### Which Agent Tasks Need a GPU


Agents need a GPU when the code they write or run assumes one. Common cases include:


- [coding agent evals](https://www.thundercompute.com/blog/coding-agent-evals-gpu-sandboxes)
- [reinforcement learning environments](https://www.thundercompute.com/blog/rl-environments-gpu-sandboxes)
- Fine-tuning or evaluating small models
- Local inference or embeddings without an external API
- Image and video generation
- Data-science notebooks that use CUDA-accelerated libraries


Running the whole agent loop in one GPU sandbox keeps the environment consistent from code generation to execution. Splitting work between a CPU sandbox and a separate GPU service adds data transfer, credentials and failure points.


### How GPU Sandbox Providers Compare


Thunder Compute, Modal, Daytona and Northflank differ more on preemption, isolation and billing than on GPU choice. Beam also offers GPU sandboxes, but Beam's GPU rates were not part of this comparison. ## Last Thoughts on E2B Alternatives


E2B remains a solid default for CPU-bound agent code execution, with microVM isolation, memory-preserving pause and an open-source core. Switching makes sense for a specific need: GPUs, cheaper idle sessions, a different persistence model, or deployment in your own cloud.


For GPU workloads, Thunder Compute offers non-preemptible, microVM-isolated A100 80GB and H100 sandboxes. Request sandbox access to try it with your agent.


## FAQ


### What Are the Best E2B Alternatives for AI Agents?


The best alternative depends on the workload. Thunder Compute fits GPU agents, and Daytona and Blaxel fit long-lived stateful agents. Northflank and Runloop fit teams that deploy into their own cloud. Vercel Sandbox and Cloudflare Sandbox SDK fit agents that mostly wait on model calls.


### Does E2B Support GPUs?


No, E2B sandboxes are CPU-only. Thunder Compute, Modal, Daytona, Northflank and Beam offer GPU sandboxes for agents that need CUDA inside the sandbox.


### Is E2B Free?


E2B has a free Hobby plan with a one-time $100 usage credit and sessions of up to one hour. After the credit runs out, vCPU and memory are billed per second. The Pro plan costs $150/month plus usage.


### How Much Does an AI Agent Sandbox Cost per Hour?


A 2 vCPU / 4 GiB sandbox costs about $0.07-$0.34/hr at list rates. Northflank is lowest at $0.0667/hr, E2B costs $0.1656/hr, and Vercel Sandbox is highest at $0.3408/hr at full CPU use.


### Which E2B Alternatives Keep State Between Sessions?


Blaxel, Daytona, CodeSandbox SDK, Fly.io Sprites and Vercel Sandbox keep state between sessions. Blaxel resumes full memory and process state in about 25 ms. Fly.io Sprites keep a persistent 100 GB filesystem, and Vercel Sandbox snapshots the filesystem on every stop.
